title: Heavy Metal Tested & Certified — published standards
description: The HMTc certification limits per product subcategory, variant, and analyte: the published limit in ppb on the row's native basis, the control basis (government-limit default, government read-across, or controlled screen), the controlling jurisdiction and instrument, and — for government-limit cells — the per-country table of sovereign limits the value was selected from. Values are set by Method v2.0 (strictest applicable government maximum level, selective occurrence for Tier-1 toxics and unregulated cells).
methodology_version: HMTc-10 / Method v2.0 — government-limit default, selective occurrence for Tier-1 toxics and unregulated cells (CLAUDE.md Part 19)

license.terms: The published HMTc standards are free to read and cite with attribution. The derivation methodology and this compiled dataset are the work of Paleo Certified, Inc., operating as the Institute of Contaminant Standards.
license.attribution: Heavy Metal Tested & Certified (HMTc), Institute of Contaminant Standards. Cite the standard's page_url and standard_version.

evidence_basis: Literature occurrence evidence the standards are checked against is reported independently at https://heavymetalindex.com and cited one-way; see each record's hmi_literature_link.

standards.name: Bread and baked goods — non-rice
standards.methodology_version: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default, 8:1 basis, read-across)

Pb.rationale: Strictest applicable government maximum level, converted to the row's native basis (Method v2.0 default).

iAs.rationale: No government sets an iAs ML for non-rice baked goods; wheat/other-grain baked products do not hyperaccumulate arsenic. Clean counterpart to rice-based products.

tAs.rationale: Strictest applicable government maximum level, converted to the row's native basis (Method v2.0 default).

tHg.rationale: Strictest applicable government maximum level, converted to the row's native basis (Method v2.0 default).

MeHg.rationale: No government sets a methylmercury ML for any grain, cereal, or rice product in any jurisdiction; methylmercury maximum levels exist only for fish and seafood. Mercury in this matrix is controlled by the total-mercury ML (30 ug/kg, Israel FCS-2016), which bounds the methylmercury fraction. Rice can accumulate trace methylmercury via paddy-soil methylation in point-source-contaminated growing re…
MeHg.reference_method: MeHg by GC-ICP-MS / EN 16801 only on a lot whose total mercury approaches the tHg ML; grain MeHg is characteristically < LOQ.

Cd.rationale: Strictest applicable government maximum level, converted to the row's native basis (Method v2.0 default).

Cr-VI.rationale: Cr-VI (hexavalent chromium): No total-Cr ML for cereal products; reflex speciation control — any total-Cr >= 100 ug/kg triggers Cr(VI) speciation, any quantifiable Cr(VI) fails.
Cr-VI.reference_method: Total-Cr by ICP-MS; Cr(VI) by EN 15192 / EPA 6800 on exceedance.

Ni.rationale: Strictest applicable government maximum level, converted to the row's native basis (Method v2.0 default).

Sn.rationale: Canned-only analyte; bread and baked goods are not sold in tinplate. Canned products route to Cat 7.

Al.basis_note: China GB 2760-2024 baked-foods Al residue 100 mg/kg (dry, as Al); Codex concurs
Al.rationale: Strictest applicable government maximum level, converted to the row's native basis (Method v2.0 default).

Pb.rationale: Strictest applicable government maximum level, converted to the row's native basis (Method v2.0 default).

iAs.rationale: Inorganic arsenic does not hyperaccumulate in wheat, corn, or other non-rice cereals as it does in rice; no government sets an iAs ML for any non-rice grain or flour in any jurisdiction. This subcategory is the clean counterpart to the rice-based flour/pasta subcategories, where iAs is the binding Tier-1 analyte.
iAs.reference_method: iAs by HPLC-ICP-MS (EN 16802) on any lot flagged for arsenic screening; non-rice grain occurrence is characteristically < LOQ.

Cr-VI.rationale: Cr-VI (hexavalent chromium): No government sets a total-chromium ML for grain/cereal products in any jurisdiction; cereal-matrix Cr is dominated by nutritionally-essential Cr(III), and Cr(VI) reduces to Cr(III) in the matrix.
